issues.title: Handler logic mixed in schema file
issues.description: The rule requires that schema and handler logic are separated into different files. However, the schema file `booking.output.ts` now contains a handler method `cleanEmailForDisplay()` that performs email validation and transformation logic, mixing schema definition with handler logic in the same file.
issues.rule_name: Schema and Handler Files Must Be Separated with Type-Safe Patterns

issues.title: Lost `this` context in displayGuests mapping causes runtime error
issues.description: In the `getOutputBooking` method at line 171, the code passes `this.getDisplayEmail` directly to the `map` function without binding the `this` context. This causes a runtime error because when `getDisplayEmail` is invoked inside the `map` callback, `this` will be `undefined`, resulting in "Cannot read property 'replace' of undefined" or similar errors. The arrow function `(guest: string) => this.getDisplayEmail(guest)` was removed, which was necessary to preserve the `this` binding. This will break all bookings that have guests.

issues.title: Recurring seated bookings returned in wrong order
issues.description: In the `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` method at line 424, the sort operation that orders bookings chronologically by start time has been removed. The original code sorted bookings with `.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime())` to ensure they are returned in chronological order. Without this sorting, recurring bookings will be returned in an arbitrary order (based on how they were stored in the database or map), which breaks the expected API contract and will confuse clients expecting chronological ordering of recurring events.

issues.title: Unnecessary regex processing on literal "unknown" string
issues.description: In the `getHost` method at line 219, when the user is null/unknown, the code now calls `this.getDisplayEmail("unknown")` instead of directly setting `displayEmail: "unknown"`. This causes unnecessary regex processing on the literal string "unknown" which has no CUID suffix to remove. While this doesn't break functionality, it adds unnecessary computational overhead and is semantically incorrect - the getDisplayEmail method is designed to strip CUID suffixes from actual email addresses, not process placeholder strings. This represents a performance issue and code smell that violates the principle of only processing data when necessary.

issues.title: Service file uses disallowed '.service.ts' suffix / naming convention violation
issues.description: Rule 1 disallows dot-suffix service filenames like '.service.ts' and requires service files to be named '<Entity>Service.ts' with matching PascalCase. This PR modifies a service located at 'services/output.service.ts', which violates the naming convention.
issues.rule_name: Rule 1: Repository and Service Classes Must Follow Naming Conventions

issues.title: Line(s) exceed the 110 character line width requirement
issues.description: The added assignment line is longer than the 110 character limit required by the Biome formatting rules for TS/JS files.
issues.rule_name: Rule 3: Use Biome for Code Formatting with Standardized Configuration

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25593 - fix(api): return original email without OAuth suffix in bookings

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds a `displayEmail` field next to the existing `email` field on hosts, attendees (regular and seated), and `reassignedTo` in API v2 2024-08-13 booking responses. It also adds `bookingFieldsResponses.displayEmail` and `displayGuests`. The new values come from a `getDisplayEmail()` helper that strips the managed-user `+{25-char cuid}` suffix. Leaving `email` as it was keeps the change backwards compatible, and the e2e coverage is broad: every existing attendee assertion was updated, and new managed-user tests cover the host, attendee, and guest cases.

One unrelated change is a real problem: the PR deletes the start-time sort from `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings`. The IDs passed in come from a Prisma query that has no `orderBy`, so recurring seated bookings can now come back out of chronological order. There are also smaller cleanup issues: an unused static helper that duplicates the regex in the shared types package, copy-pasted post-processing blocks that don't match each other, an OpenAPI file that looks hand-edited (broken indentation), and a regex that isn't anchored to the `@`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `displayEmail` feature itself is sound and well tested. But removing the sort in `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` is an unrelated behavior regression: GET of a recurring seated booking can return occurrences in random order. It needs to be restored before merge.

architecture.overview:
API v2 booking endpoints (2024-08-13) delegate response shaping to `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13`. That service maps Prisma `Booking` rows (with user, attendees, seats) into DTOs defined in `@calcom/platform-types` (`BookingOutput_2024_08_13`, `RecurringBookingOutput_2024_08_13`, seated variants, `ReassignBookingOutput_2024_08_13`) using `plainToClass` with `excludeAll`. Because of that, only `@Expose()`d fields survive. `bookingFieldsResponses` and `metadata` are attached by hand afterward.

The PR adds a private `getDisplayEmail()` regex helper and calls it everywhere an email is put into the output: `getHost`, each attendee mapper, and `getOutputReassignedBooking`. It also post-processes `bookingFieldsResponses` to add `displayEmail` and `displayGuests`. The DTO classes get matching `@Expose()`d `displayEmail` properties so they survive `plainToClass`, and the OpenAPI spec and oasdiff ignore list were updated. Separately, the PR drops the chronological sort in `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings`.
steps: Start at `BookingsService_2024_08_13.getBooking` (bookings.service.ts ~L590-615). It routes to the regular, recurring, seated, or recurring-seated output builders.
Read `getDisplayEmail` (output.service.ts L96-98). It's a regex that strips the first `+` followed by 25 alphanumerics, the same pattern used in google-calendar.service.ts.
Follow how it's applied: `getHost` (L213-229), the attendee mappers (L131-139, L275-282, L383-392, L512-521), and `getOutputReassignedBooking` (L539-553).
Look at the post-`plainToClass` mutation of `bookingFieldsResponses` that adds `displayEmail`/`displayGuests` (L158-174, L303-319).
Check the DTO changes in packages/platform/types/.../booking.output.ts: `@Expose() displayEmail` on BookingAttendee, BookingHost, and ReassignedToDto.
Note the unrelated change in `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` (L411-425): the `.sort()` by start time was removed.

findings.title: Removing the sort makes recurring seated bookings come back out of order
findings.fixPrompt: In apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts, `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` (around line 424) used to return `transformed.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime())`. This PR changed it to `return transformed;`. Restore the sort so recurring seated bookings come back in chronological order, matching `getOutputRecurringBookings` and `getOutputCreateRecurringSeatedBookings` in the same file. The IDs come from a repository query with no orderBy, so you can't rely on their order.

findings.title: Unused `cleanEmailForDisplay` static duplicates the regex in the shared types package
findings.fixPrompt: In packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts lines 58-62, delete the unused static method `BookingAttendee.cleanEmailForDisplay` and its comment. Nothing references it, and it duplicates `getDisplayEmail` in apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts. Keep the DTO classes free of logic.

findings.title: Copy-pasted bookingFieldsResponses post-processing, and the two copies differ
findings.fixPrompt: In apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts, the blocks that add `displayEmail`/`displayGuests` to `bookingFieldsResponses` are duplicated at lines ~158-174 (getOutputBooking) and ~303-319 (getOutputRecurringBooking). One uses an unbound `this.getDisplayEmail` reference in `.map`. Pull this logic into one private helper method that takes the responses object, uses an arrow function for the guests map, and is called from both places.

findings.title: CUID regex isn't anchored to the `@` and can mangle legitimate plus-addressed emails
findings.fixPrompt: In apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts line 97, `getDisplayEmail` uses `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}/`. That can strip part of a longer plus-tag (e.g. `a+<25 alnum>2024@x.com` becomes `a2024@x.com`). Anchor it with a lookahead, `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}(?=@)/`, so it only removes a suffix that sits right before the `@`. Add a unit test for normal emails, managed-user emails, and long plus-tags.

findings.title: openapi.json looks hand-edited, with broken indentation on `required`
findings.fixPrompt: docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json has four `"required": [` lines (around 31729, 31833, 32267, 33370) with the indentation stripped, which suggests manual edits. Regenerate the OpenAPI spec with the api/v2 swagger generation script so the file matches the `@ApiProperty` decorators in packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts and is formatted consistently.

findings.title: The fix is additive and doesn't break existing clients
findings.body: Keeping `email` unchanged and adding `displayEmail` alongside it means platform customers who match on the suffixed address keep working. The DTOs mark the new field with `@Expose()`, so it survives `plainToClass({ strategy: "excludeAll" })`. It's also applied in every output path, including seated attendees and `reassignedTo`.

findings.title: Good e2e coverage of the new field
findings.body: Every existing attendee `toEqual` assertion was updated, so the new field is checked across user, team, org, recurring, seated, and reassign flows. The new tests in managed-user-bookings.e2e-spec.ts check the host, attendee, `bookingFieldsResponses.email`, and guests cases against real managed users with CUID suffixes. Those tests check both sides: `email` keeps the suffix and `displayEmail` drops it.
